output.summary: The evidence leans hawkish for the 2026-10-28 decision. The Committee hiked 25 bp in September by a 12-0 vote, the tone read scored maximally hawkish (score 1.0, no dovish terms), and the minutes state most participants expected another increase would likely be appropriate by year end. The September SEP implies about 22.5 bp of further tightening across the two remaining meetings, and base-rate history conditional on the last hike puts hike probability at 0.653 versus 0.347 for a hold. Post-meeting speeches reinforce this: Waller anticipates additional hikes if data hold, and Jefferson sees inflation risks tilted to the upside; inflation remains ~1.0 pp above goal while unemployment sits at the natural rate (gap 0.0). Counterweights are modest: two-year yields fell 20 bp over four weeks, and Chair Warsh stressed data dependence and declined to prejudge future actions, and only ~0.9 moves are implied over two meetings so an October move is not certain. Net tilt +6 bp (hawkish).

output.summary: All evidence points the same direction ahead of the 2026-10-28 decision: hawkish, i.e. toward another rate increase. The September meeting was a unanimous 12–0 hike with a hawkish statement rewrite; the SEP median moved up and implies roughly one more quarter-point move across the two remaining 2026 meetings; the base-rate history shows a 0.653 hike probability conditional on a prior hike; and officials (Waller, Jefferson, Cook, Warsh) plus the minutes signal more firming is likely "by year end." The only tempering signals are that hikes "do not need to come at consecutive meetings," Warsh's refusal to give forward guidance, and softening payrolls (3-month average below breakeven), which keep an October move from being certain. Net: clearly hawkish lean, +7 bp.
